chosen.premise: When Psyduck has a headache, its brain cells become 10 times more active.
chosen.hook: A Psyduck headache makes its brain work ten times harder.
chosen.visualIdea: Split-screen: normal Psyduck brain activity versus a headache state labeled 10×.
chosen.note: The exact 10× figure gives this a powerful short-form hook and clear visual comparison. It is strongly supported by one explicit Pokédex entry, though it is more about brain activity than a fully explained mechanic.

candidates.premise: Psyduck can unleash mystical powers, then forget that it ever used them.
candidates.hook: Psyduck’s biggest attacks leave no memory behind.
candidates.visualIdea: A psychic blast hits, then the scene rewinds as Psyduck looks around confused.
candidates.note: The combination of unleashing psychic power and forming no memory of it is a distinctive contradiction with strong multi-entry support. The premise could be made even sharper by emphasizing the missing memory immediately after the attack.

candidates.premise: When Psyduck finally lets its strange power erupt, the psychic release can ease its headache temporarily.
candidates.hook: For Psyduck, a psychic explosion is temporary pain relief.
candidates.visualIdea: A headache meter peaks, a psychic wave erupts, and the meter briefly drops.
candidates.note: The contradiction that Psyduck’s psychic eruption temporarily relieves the pain causing it is an excellent episode premise. Support comes from two entries, but one says 'apparently,' so the claim should retain that uncertainty.

candidates.premise: The worse Psyduck’s headache gets, the more powerful its psychokinesis becomes.
candidates.hook: Psyduck’s superpower runs on worsening pain.
candidates.visualIdea: A headache gauge rises while Psyduck’s psychic energy grows stronger.
candidates.note: The pain-to-power mechanic is highly specific to Psyduck, clearly supported by the Moon entry, and easy to animate. It is slightly less surprising because the headache-power connection is central to Psyduck’s established identity.

candidates.premise: Psyduck’s psychic power appears during an altered state resembling deep sleep.
candidates.hook: Psyduck’s psychic attacks happen while its brain acts asleep.
candidates.visualIdea: Psyduck’s eyes droop as a sleep-like brain graphic transforms into a psychic blast.
candidates.note: A psychic Pokémon whose powers emerge during a sleep-like altered state is unusual and visually rich. The wording combines several entries and slightly blurs whether Psyduck is literally asleep, so support is strong but not absolute.

candidates.premise: Psyduck’s psychic power is triggered by agony and stress, often without its intention.
candidates.hook: Psyduck doesn’t choose when its psychic power goes off.
candidates.visualIdea: Stress and pain indicators stack up until Psyduck accidentally overwhelms everything nearby.
candidates.note: The loss-of-control angle is supported and easy to stage, but it overlaps heavily with Psyduck’s general headache lore. 'Triggered by agony and stress' also compresses several descriptions rather than presenting one especially sharp rule.

rounds.request: N/A—the 10× brain-activity angle is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally concrete numerical or contradictory fact, with explicit Pokédex support and a visual mechanic that can be understood instantly.
